answer: We score influence by conviction: tokens times unbroken lock time, not wallet count. A gale of fresh addresses changes nothing, because each empty key starts at zero and must keep capital locked for many epochs before its vote counts. Splitting a treasury into a plume of tiny balances hurts the attacker: every shard resets its timer and never catches one concentrated lock. The reputation map is a karst: shallow underfunded sinkholes drain away, while only deep channels of long-locked tokens carry weight. The real bill is buying those tokens and waiting; extra identities are free but useless.
